record.title: Cyber Bureau busts SMC app Ponzi scheme; Chinese national among 11 held
record.detail: Nepal Police Cyber Bureau arrested 11 people incl. a Chinese national over the 'SMC' movie-trailer app promising 1.2% daily returns; police said over 70,000 users lost about Rs120.8 million. Arrests in Kathmandu, Tarakeshwar, Birgunj and Butwal.

record.title: Bus plunges off Prithvi Highway toward Trishuli; 19 dead
record.detail: A passenger bus left the Prithvi Highway and fell down a slope near the Trishuli River in Dhading, killing at least 19 including a British national and injuring 25.

record.title: Nepal–India border sealed 72 hours for general election
record.detail: Cross-border movement of people and goods except essentials was halted from Monday midnight for 72 hours ahead of the 5 March House of Representatives election under the Integrated Security Plan, enforced by the Armed Police Force.

record.title: Three Nepalis rescued from Myawaddy scam centres flown home
record.detail: The Embassy of Nepal in Bangkok, with Myanmar and Thai authorities, repatriated three Nepalis forced to work in online scam operations in Myawaddy, Myanmar.

record.title: 21 Nepalis from Bavet casino-scam complex repatriated
record.detail: 21 of 30 Nepalis detained in a 28 January Cambodian police raid on a Bavet casino complex (over 2,000 foreigners held) were repatriated, coordinated by the Nepali embassy in Bangkok and NRNA Cambodia.

record.title: Air Dynasty helicopter crash-lands in Khotang
record.detail: An Air Dynasty helicopter (9N-AFQ) crash-landed at Belabesi, Khotang; one passenger injured, pilot and four others safe. The operator cited strong wind and dust; investigation pending.
record.attribution: Operator manager via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: CIAA charges ex-Speaker Mahara in 9 kg vape-gold smuggling case
record.detail: CIAA filed charges at the Special Court against former Speaker Krishna Bahadur Mahara over about 9 kg of gold hidden in 730 e-cigarettes at TIA in 2022, seeking recovery of Rs77.86 million; CIB also pursues organised-crime charges.
record.attribution: Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority

record.title: Kathmandu ranks among world's 10 most polluted cities
record.detail: IQAir reported Kathmandu's AQI above 190 ('unhealthy'), citing wildfires and agricultural burning, vehicle and brick-kiln emissions and valley topography.

record.title: 612 Nepalis rescued from SE Asian scam hubs; 14 detained in Cambodia
record.detail: MoFA said 612 Nepalis had been rescued and repatriated (Cambodia 487, Myanmar 111, Laos 8, Thailand 6); 9 more Nepalis were arrested in Cambodia on fraud, hostage-taking and torture allegations, bringing those detained there to 14.
record.attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Paudel Chhetri

record.title: Nepal sends notes to India and China over Lipulekh route
record.detail: MoFA sent diplomatic notes to India and China objecting to reopening the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage/trade route via Lipulekh, restating that Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh and Kalapani belong to Nepal under the 1816 Sugauli Treaty.
record.attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri

record.title: APG warns Nepal of blacklist risk over slow AML reforms
record.detail: An APG delegation led by Deputy Executive Secretary David Shannon found meaningful progress on only 9 of 15 FATF action items and warned failure could lead to blacklisting; it also questioned May 2026 amendments expanding DMLI powers. Exit deadline February 2027.
record.attribution: APG delegation via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: 71 more rescued; scam-centre repatriations total 687
record.detail: MoFA reported 71 more Nepalis rescued, taking the total to 687 (Cambodia 562); the Bangkok embassy secured fine waivers for 102 from Cambodia with 172 pending, while 29 Nepalis remained detained in Cambodia on organised-crime and trafficking charges.
record.attribution: MoFA spokesperson Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri

record.title: DHM forecasts below-normal, hotter monsoon
record.detail: DHM's National Outlook for Monsoon Season 2026 forecast below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures across most of Nepal due to El Niño, while warning intense localised rain can still cause floods and landslides.

record.title: 23 arrested with drugs across seven districts
record.detail: Nepal Police arrested 23 people with brown sugar, cannabis and prescription tablets, 11 of them in Kathmandu and 6 in Jhapa.

record.title: Nepal stays on FATF grey list after June review
record.detail: FATF kept Nepal under increased monitoring; outstanding items include risk-based supervision of banks, cooperatives, casinos and real estate, more ML prosecutions, and sanctioning illegal money transfer (hundi) services.
record.attribution: FATF review report via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: 775 kg of marijuana found under potato sacks in Koshi
record.detail: Koshi Province Police arrested five and seized 795 kg of marijuana, 775 kg of it in a mini-truck intercepted at Sangurigadhi RM, Dhankuta.
record.attribution: SSP Yogendra Singh Thapa, Koshi Province Police

record.title: Monsoon landslides kill infant in Dolakha and woman in Jajarkot
record.detail: Rain-triggered landslides killed a four-month-old in Kalinchok, Dolakha and a 60-year-old woman in Bheri Municipality, Jajarkot on 12–13 July, per local reports.
record.attribution: Local officials via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: Tatopani crossing shut as Araniko/Kodari Highway subsides
record.detail: The Tatopani–Zhangmu crossing closed after the Kodari Highway subsided about two metres at Iko, Bhotekoshi RM, leaving dozens of cargo containers stuck on the Chinese side.
record.attribution: Local officials via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: DHM warns of heavy to very heavy rain in six provinces
record.detail: DHM warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall over 19–20 July in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini and Sudurpaschim, citing a Bay of Bengal low and a northward monsoon trough; flood, landslide and urban inundation risk flagged.

record.title: Communal unrest in Sunsari and Siraha leaves three dead; curfew
record.detail: A Hindu–Muslim dispute over music and flags during a procession escalated; police shot two men in Sunsari and one man died in a Siraha protest. Curfew imposed in Sunsari and neighbouring areas; PM Balendra Shah appealed for calm and promised an investigation.
record.attribution: Nepal Police and PM Balendra Shah, via Al Jazeera

record.title: Susta standoff after SSB dismantles flood embankment
record.detail: Indian SSB personnel dismantled a makeshift earthen flood embankment built by residents in disputed Susta; Indian side said a crowd of 150–200 pelted stones at the patrol, no injuries reported. Nepal's APF intervened and Kathmandu raised the matter with New Delhi.
record.agency: Armed Police Force; Sashastra Seema Bal
record.attribution: CDO Dipak Raj Nepal via The Kathmandu Post; SSB account via ETV Bharat

record.title: NCB Nepalgunj seizes 579 g brown sugar sourced from India
record.detail: Narcotics Control Bureau's Nepalgunj office arrested two men with nearly 579 g of brown sugar, Rs180,000 and INR 214,000; police said it was sourced from Bahraich, India for Karnali and Lumbini.

record.title: Glacier collapse triggers catastrophic Rasuwa–Trishuli flood
record.detail: A glacial collapse sent ice, rock and debris into the Lhende Khola, unleashing a flood down the Bhotekoshi/Trishuli valley that destroyed the Gyirong/Rasuwagadhi border area; at least 469 deaths in Nepal were reported by 28 August, with over 1,500 missing across Nepal and Tibet.

record.title: USGS characterises Langtang debris avalanche
record.detail: USGS said the event was likely triggered by rapid slope failure involving a glacier in Langtang National Park, releasing energy equal to an M5.2 quake with a secondary M4.2 signal three hours later, and travelling about 100 km downstream past the Rasuwagadhi border post.

record.title: Flood destroys Rasuwagadhi–Kerung crossing, Nepal's main China trade gateway
record.detail: The flood destroyed the Rasuwagadhi checkpoint, Sino-Nepal Friendship Bridge and dry port; the route had carried 60–70 cargo vehicles a day, and customs officials said about 176 containers were stranded in Kerung, with trade to be rerouted via Tatopani or Korala.
record.attribution: Customs officials via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: China warns of barrier lake upstream of Bhotekoshi
record.detail: China's Ministry of Water Resources warned via CCTV that a ~2 million cubic metre barrier lake near the Chhochen Khola–Purepu Tsangpo confluence was overflowing and at high risk of breaching, with 3 million m3 more inflow expected; Nepali authorities restricted highway movement and moved residents downstream.
record.attribution: China Ministry of Water Resources via CCTV, reported by The Kathmandu Post

record.title: Flood wrecks hydropower, roads; reconstruction put at $4–5bn
record.detail: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle gave a preliminary reconstruction estimate of US$4–5 billion (about Rs762 billion); roughly 15,000 houses destroyed, multiple hydropower plants damaged and road links to Dhunche and Syafrubesi severed; NDRRMA rapid assessment under way, PDNA expected to take two months.
record.attribution: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and NPC Vice-chair Gunakhar Bhatta, via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: Bhotekoshi–Trishuli flood toll reaches 1,355
record.detail: NDRRMA put the toll at 1,355 dead, 6,672 treated for injuries and 4,996 unaccounted for across eight districts (Chitwan 363 deaths, Nawalparasi East 222, Nawalparasi West 221), with 13,396 rescued; preliminary losses Rs387.5 billion (about US$2.56 billion).
record.attribution: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, via The Kathmandu Post

record.title: Gen Z uprising anniversary gathering in Baneshwar
record.detail: Gen Z activists and victims' families gathered at the former Parliament building to mark one year since the September 2025 uprising; PM Shah was absent and Home Minister Sudan Gurung attended. Karki Commission recommendations remain largely unprosecuted.

record.title: Heavy to very heavy rain forecast for 24–28 September
record.detail: DHM's Meteorological Forecasting Division warned of heavy to very heavy rain over 24–28 September, heaviest in western and central Nepal; some models showed 400–741 mm. The 2026 monsoon entered Nepal on 19 June, six days late.
record.attribution: DHM Meteorological Forecasting Division; model figures per meteorologist Binod Pokharel

record.title: First Australian payment to Nauru under NZYQ deportee deal
record.detail: ABC reported the Australian government made its first payment to Nauru under the deal to resettle NZYQ-cohort non-citizens, and faced questions over it.

record.title: Claims of threats against NZYQ deportees in Nauru
record.detail: An Australian MP used parliamentary privilege to relay a whistleblower's claims of threats and violence against NZYQ deportees in Nauru (claims, not verified).

record.title: Pacific leaders call Chinese missile test 'reckless'
record.detail: ABC reports Pacific leaders, including from Nauru and Tuvalu, criticised a Chinese nuclear-capable missile test as reckless.

record.title: Nauru (Naoero) and Kiribati stir frustration over China at the Forum
record.detail: ABC reports Naoero and Kiribati caused frustration at the Pacific Islands Forum over their positions on China.

record.title: 18 kg of meth found on passenger from Singapore
record.detail: Customs said a 33-year-old NZ national arriving at Auckland Airport from Singapore had 18.45 kg of methamphetamine (street value about NZ$5.53 million) and was charged.

record.title: Glue drum explodes at Motueka wood-products site
record.detail: A glue drum exploded at a wood product manufacturing facility on Little Sydney Rd near Motueka; one worker was taken to Nelson Hospital in a serious condition. WorkSafe was notified and made initial inquiries.
record.agency: WorkSafe; Fire and Emergency NZ; St John
record.attribution: Per St John and WorkSafe as reported by 1News

record.title: Eleven vegetation fires in Canterbury; 22 ha burn near Napier
record.detail: Fire and Emergency NZ fought 11 vegetation fires across Canterbury, with 20 trucks and three helicopters at the Rotherham fire at peak; near Napier a Waitara Road fire burned 22 ha (18 ha plantation, 4 ha DOC bush). Heat and strong winds drove the blazes.
record.attribution: Per Fire and Emergency NZ as reported by 1News

record.title: Storm landslides kill 8 in Bay of Plenty; 9 dead in January system
record.detail: A subtropical low brought states of emergency to Whangārei, Thames-Coromandel, Hauraki, Bay of Plenty and Tairāwhiti; 1News reports six killed by a landslide at a Mount Maunganui holiday park, two in a Pāpāmoa house and one man swept away near Warkworth.
record.attribution: Civil Defence declarations and death toll via 1News

record.title: Record-setting rain: 274 mm in a day at Tauranga
record.detail: NIWA's January summary says tropical air on 18-22 January brought record-setting rainfall and flooding to much of the North Island and upper South Island; the month's highest 1-day total was 274 mm at Tauranga on 21 January, and Coromandel, Bay of Plenty and North Canterbury had 300-400%+ of normal January rain. (NIWA's page does not give a Whitianga figure.)
record.attribution: Climate data per NIWA monthly climate summary

record.title: NZ-supported Pacific op intercepts 4.2 t of cocaine
record.detail: Customs said Operation Kiwa, with NZDF and GCSB support, helped French authorities seize 4.24 tonnes (174 bales) of cocaine on the high seas off French Polynesia.

record.title: Woman arrested over alleged 18-year romance scam
record.detail: Police said a 44-year-old Auckland woman was charged with obtaining by deception after allegedly taking NZ$525,537 from a Dunedin victim in a romance scam dating back to 2006.

record.title: SH39 bridge near Puketotara collapses; ute drives into gap
record.detail: State Highway 39 Bridge 520, south of Mangati Road near Puketotara north of Ōtorohanga, partly collapsed in flooding after about 250-300 mm of rain in eight hours; a ute drove into the washout overnight and the occupant escaped unhurt.
record.attribution: As reported by NZ Herald; rainfall estimate per the report

record.title: Man dies in submerged vehicle on SH39; Ōtorohanga emergency
record.detail: A man was found dead in his vehicle after it was submerged by floodwaters on State Highway 39; Ōtorohanga Mayor Rodney Dow declared a district state of emergency and about 80 people were evacuated, many to Te Kotahitanga Marae. (The earlier summary's 'ute swept off SH39' is not how 1News or NZ Herald describe it: the fatality was a submerged vehicle near the Kiwi Road intersection, while a separate ute drove into a collapsed bridge and its occupant escaped.)
record.attribution: Per Ōtorohanga District Council and police as reported by 1News

record.title: Storm brings 240 km/h gust at Cape Turnagain; 30,000+ lose power
record.detail: Gusts reached 240 km/h at Cape Turnagain, up to 190 km/h on Wellington's high ground and about 130 km/h in the city; more than 30,000 properties lost power, about 23,000 on the Powerco network and about 10,000 in Wellington. Air New Zealand cancelled flights including Wellington services.
record.attribution: Wind and outage figures as reported by Anadolu, citing RNZ and Powerco

record.title: Storm disrupts flights, trains and ferries; Air NZ pauses three airports
record.detail: Reuters reported the storm disrupted flights, trains and ferries; Air New Zealand paused operations at Wellington, Napier and Palmerston North, with a few Wellington flights resuming by afternoon while cancellations stayed widespread. More than 30,000 properties were without power. (Reuters gives no operator-level train or Cook Strait ferry figures.)

record.title: Two travel-linked measles cases in Auckland household
record.detail: Health NZ confirmed two measles cases in one Auckland household linked to overseas travel; locations of interest included flight SQ281 from Singapore (arrived 17 February), Auckland Airport and Waitakere Hospital's emergency waiting room on 21 February.
record.attribution: Per Health NZ Medical Officer of Health as reported by 1News

record.title: Spark to block ~300 phones that cannot call 111 after 3G shutdown
record.detail: Spark said it would block about 300 mobile phones, mainly ASUS models, that cannot make emergency 111 calls once its 3G network shuts on 31 March 2026, calling them a significant safety risk; One NZ and 2degrees are also closing 3G.

record.title: Smuggled jewelled geckos repatriated from Netherlands
record.detail: DOC said six jewelled geckos seized by Dutch authorities in a 2023 Interpol-backed operation were repatriated; DOC said the species has never been legally exported, implying smuggling.

record.title: Emborg Emmentaler cheese recalled over Listeria
record.detail: New Zealand Food Safety recalled a batch of Emborg Emmentaler 200 g cheese (best before 4 November 2026) sold at supermarkets nationwide over possible Listeria; no illnesses were mentioned.
record.attribution: Recall notice by NZ Food Safety as reported by 1News

record.title: Meningococcal B cases among Dunedin students treated as outbreak
record.detail: Health NZ is treating two meningococcal B cases among Dunedin students (Otago Polytechnic hall on 7 March and University of Otago) as an outbreak; pharmacies reported high vaccine demand and some ran out of stock.
record.attribution: Per Health NZ as reported by 1News

record.title: Red heavy rain warning for eastern Northland
record.detail: MetService issued a Red warning (third of 2026) for Northland east of Kaikohe, Doubtless Bay to Whangārei, from 16:00 25 Mar to 04:00 27 Mar, forecasting 270-320 mm with peak rates of 25-40 mm/h from a subtropical low.

record.title: About 500 evacuated in Kaitāia as rivers flood
record.detail: Around 500 people left homes near the Awanui and Pairatahi river confluence after roughly two months' rain fell in 24 hours; states of emergency were declared in Far North and Whangārei districts, with FENZ and USAR rescuing residents.

record.title: Boil-water notice for four Auckland suburbs lifted
record.detail: Watercare lifted a two-day boil-water notice for Hillsborough, Mt Roskill, Royal Oak and Three Kings after tracing E. coli detections to a single faulty water-quality sampling tap, which was replaced; thousands of residents had been affected.

record.title: Waikato state of emergency for Cyclone Vaianu
record.detail: Waikato CDEM declared a seven-day state of emergency at 09:32 on 11 Apr, ended 13 Apr; Port Waikato residents were displaced and SH25 was closed by slips between Coromandel Town–Whangapoua and Manaia–Thames.

record.title: Cyclone Vaianu crosses coast near Maketu, Bay of Plenty
record.detail: Reuters reported Vaianu made landfall on Sunday near the Maketu Peninsula in the Bay of Plenty, triggering floods, power outages and hundreds of evacuations; Whangārei had over 100 mm in 24 hours per MetService. (Corrects earlier 'landfall in Northland' dated 11 April.)

record.title: Air NZ cancels 90+ regional turboprop flights for Vaianu
record.detail: Air New Zealand cancelled more than 90 turboprop flights from regional North Island airports while jets and international services ran with delays; 270 mandatory evacuations were ordered in Whakatāne District and about 5,000 homes lost power.
record.attribution: Reuters report republished by Malay Mail

record.title: NZDF rejects China claims over P-8A flight
record.detail: NZDF said its P-8A Poseidon crew operated professionally and lawfully while monitoring North Korea sanctions evasion over the Yellow Sea and East China Sea, and that it had no data indicating disruption to civil aviation, after Chinese claims about the flight.

record.title: Wellington state of emergency after 77 mm in an hour
record.detail: Wellington Regional Emergency Management declared a state of emergency at 14:30 on 20 Apr after the mayor cited 77 mm of rain in one hour at one site; Wainuiomata streets were evacuated, about 10 houses became uninhabitable and FENZ fielded 180+ calls in one morning.
record.attribution: WREMO, Wellington mayor and FENZ via The Spinoff

record.title: Wellington flood cancels flights and ferries
record.detail: 28 flights were cancelled at Wellington Airport, all Metlink harbour ferries were cancelled for two days, SH2 was cut to one lane near Melling and Riverside Drive in Lower Hutt closed.
record.attribution: Airport, Metlink and NZTA information via The Spinoff

record.title: Body of missing man found after Wellington floods
record.detail: Police found the body of a man missing since the floods in Karori; his car had been found in Karori Stream. Newtown and Island Bay businesses were damaged and shelters were opened.

record.title: RNZAF P-8A spots possible DPRK sanctions breach
record.detail: NZDF said an RNZAF P-8A patrol over the Yellow Sea and East China Sea recorded a possible ship-to-ship transfer in breach of UN sanctions on North Korea, logged 35 vessels of interest and broadcast 8 deterrence messages.

record.title: 39 kg of meth seized at Wellington Airport
record.detail: Customs said two women aged 21 and 22 arriving from Malaysia via Sydney had 39 kg of methamphetamine (up to NZ$13 million) disguised as tea in suitcases; both were charged with importing a Class A drug.

record.title: NZDF and Customs fly Pacific surveillance under Operation Kiwa
record.detail: NZDF said an MC-12K and a P-8A patrolled the EEZs of Fiji, Niue and the Cook Islands in May under the Customs-led Operation Kiwa against transnational crime, photographing vessels possibly engaged in illegal activity for follow-up.
record.agency: New Zealand Defence Force / NZ Customs

record.title: 100 kg of cocaine found in Tauranga reefer container
record.detail: Customs said x-ray found 100 kg of cocaine (up to NZ$35 million) hidden by rip-on/rip-off in a container loaded in Chile via Peru, Colombia and Panama at the Port of Tauranga.

record.title: Anti-Scam Alliance widens bank, telco and platform measures
record.detail: Minister Cameron Brewer announced wider Confirmation of Payee, an Online Scams Code backed by Google, Meta and TikTok, and a telco blocking code; a six-month pilot blocked 23,000+ domains and prevented about NZ$23.8 million in losses. MBIE cites NZ$265 million in bank-reported fraud losses in the year to Oct 2025.
record.attribution: Minister and Anti-Scam Alliance via SecurityBrief

record.title: NCSC Q1: NZ$5.6m lost, first 'highly significant' incidents since 2021/22
record.detail: NCSC handled 1,164 reports in Jan-Mar 2026 with NZ$5.6 million direct loss (NZ$5.2 million from individuals); three C2 incidents were the first of that class since 2021/22.

record.title: DIA issues formal AML warnings to 10 reporting entities
record.detail: DIA, sole AML/CFT supervisor from 1 July 2026, issued formal warnings to six Auckland law firms and a payment provider, real estate agent, accountant and lender for failing to get required independent audits.

record.title: About 200 Wellington flights cancelled in southerly storm
record.detail: Around 200 flights were cancelled at Wellington Airport as winds near 100 km/h hit, with gusts over 150 km/h at Mt Kaukau; SH2 near Kaitoke was blocked by a fallen tree and more than 4,000 properties lost power on the Wellington Electricity network.
record.attribution: Per Wellington Airport and Wellington Electricity as reported by 1News

record.title: 7,000+ lower North Island customers lose power in storm
record.detail: More than 7,000 customers in the lower North Island lost power: 5,280 on the Powerco network (3,000+ in Taranaki, 1,300+ in Whanganui) and 1,789 in Wellington; about 200 flights were grounded and ferry sailings cancelled.
record.attribution: Outage figures per lines companies as reported by Insurance Business

record.title: 24 arrested, NZ$1.95m assets seized in Waikato gang probe
record.detail: Police said an investigation into Comanchero, Mongols and Mongrel Mob members in Waikato and Auckland led to 24 arrests and seizure of NZ$1.95 million in assets, 2.5 kg meth, 134 kg pseudoephedrine intercepted by Customs and firearms.

record.title: Red rain warning for coastal Dunedin and Clutha
record.detail: MetService issued a Red Heavy Rain Warning from noon 5 Jul to 09:00 6 Jul for coastal Dunedin and Clutha, forecasting 80-120 mm; Otago Regional Council flagged Taieri Plains, Milton and the Clutha Delta for flooding and Dunedin's EOC was activated.
record.attribution: MetService warning via Otago Regional Council

record.title: First H5N1 bird flu confirmed in NZ, in skua at Petone
record.detail: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b was confirmed in a brown skua found on Petone Beach, Wellington, New Zealand's first detection; MPI widened wildlife surveillance. Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said the public health risk is low.
record.attribution: Per MPI and the Biosecurity Minister as reported by 1News

record.title: M5.9 quake north of Te Anau prompts brief tsunami alert
record.detail: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake (first assessed as 6.3) struck about 40 km north of Te Anau at 21:14 NZST; NEMA issued then cancelled a tsunami alert after no signals were detected. More than 18,000 felt reports went to GeoNet, with no immediate damage or injuries reported.
record.attribution: Per GeoNet and NEMA as reported by SBS

record.title: Fake-police callers draining crypto holders
record.detail: Police warned of a rise in calls from fake detectives who steer victims to fake crypto sites to harvest seed phrases; Police said some victims lost millions.

record.title: M5.9 Taumarunui quake, largest recorded there; highways shut by slips
record.detail: A shallow magnitude 5.9 quake (9 km deep) struck 5 km south-west of Taumarunui at 04:51, felt by over 22,000 people; windows broke and stock fell but no injuries were reported. 79 aftershocks followed within hours, and SH3 through the Awakino Gorge and SH43 were closed.
record.agency: GeoNet (Earth Sciences New Zealand); NZ Transport Agency
record.attribution: Per GeoNet seismologists as reported by 1News

record.title: Christchurch man faces trafficking, migrant exploitation charges
record.detail: Immigration NZ laid 35 charges under the Crimes and Immigration Acts, including trafficking in persons, against a Christchurch man over alleged exploitation of 11 victims.

record.title: Auckland flu admissions highest since 2015
record.detail: Health NZ said 177 people were admitted with flu to four Auckland hospitals in 9-16 August, up from 125 the week before and the highest weekly rate since 2015, driven by influenza A(H3N2) subclade K alongside RSV and rhinovirus.
record.attribution: Admission figures per Health NZ as reported by 1News

record.title: NCSC Q2: scams lead incident reports; losses fall to NZ$2.7m
record.detail: NCSC handled 1,129 reports in Apr-Jun 2026; scams and fraud were the top category (348 reports, about NZ$860,000 lost) and total direct loss fell 52% to NZ$2.7 million. It flagged QR-code phishing at Christchurch parking meters.

record.title: Transpower grid fault cuts power to 25,000 in Southland
record.detail: A national grid fault on the Transpower network around midday cut power to about 25,000 PowerNet customers in Southland and parts of Otago for about two hours, during an orange wind warning with lightning damage; about 300 remained off that evening.
record.attribution: Per Transpower and PowerNet as reported by 1News

record.title: Scrub fire at Albert Town, Wānaka, forces 22 households out
record.detail: A fire through about 1 km of trees and scrub behind houses at Albert Town was fought by eight crews in windy conditions; 22 households were evacuated as a precaution and no houses burned. It was contained by 23:00; the cause was unknown.
record.agency: Fire and Emergency New Zealand; Police

record.title: Trans-Tasman crackdown: 85 NZ raids, 34 charged
record.detail: Police said a 14-18 Sep joint NZ-Australia operation produced 85 raids and 34 people charged in NZ, seizing 6,183 cannabis plants, 30 kg meth, opium, 4 firearms and NZ$647,690 cash; Auckland grow houses were linked to Vietnamese organised crime.

record.title: NZ warships transit Taiwan Strait, reportedly tracked by PLA
record.detail: NZDF confirmed HMNZS Te Mana and HMNZS Aotearoa transited the Taiwan Strait during a three-month deployment; Chinese forces reportedly tracked the ships.
record.attribution: NZDF confirmation via Stuff; tracking claim is reported

record.title: Head Hunters case: laundering via crypto accounts alleged
record.detail: Court documents in Police's Operation Juneau allege North Shore Head Hunters proceeds were laundered through financial and crypto accounts, funding luxury travel and a Dubai car-hire business; a founding member charged with money laundering has pleaded not guilty, trial March 2027.
record.agency: NZ Police National Organised Crime Group

record.title: 2025 record for Chinese coast guard presence near Senkakus
record.detail: Japan Coast Guard data reported Chinese coast guard vessels were sighted near the Senkakus 357 times in 2025, a record for the fourth straight year, with 27 entries into territorial waters. The 11th Regional Coast Guard commander called the situation 'increasingly severe'.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Record ~6kg meth seizure at Naha Airport announced
record.detail: Okinawa District Customs and prefectural police said a 27-year-old man arriving from Bangkok (Don Mueang) on Sept 30, 2025 carried about 5.95kg of methamphetamine, worth about ¥340 million, in candy and detergent boxes; the largest seizure at Naha Airport.
record.agency: Okinawa District Customs / Okinawa Prefectural Police
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Six including Kyokuryukai executive held over labour dispatch to US base sites
record.detail: Organized crime police arrested six people including a senior figure of designated gang Kyokuryukai, alleging 25 workers were illegally dispatched 819 times to 114 sites incl. Kadena Air Base and public works between April 2023 and July 2025.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Four Chinese warships transit Miyako Strait
record.detail: Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force tracked two Chinese guided-missile destroyers, a frigate and a replenishment ship passing between Okinawa and Miyako Island into the Philippine Sea overnight (Tuesday evening to early Wednesday), per Japan's Joint Staff.
record.attribution: Japan Joint Staff via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Three foreigners caught with THC gummies at Naha Airport
record.detail: Customs found THC gummies on a Brazilian couple resident in Okinawa City (2.18g) and a US man from Michigan (~78g) arriving from Bangkok; all three were arrested/charged under the narcotics law, with charges filed by customs.
record.agency: Okinawa District Customs / Tomigusuku Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Tomigusuku Police Station

record.title: Foam from sewer manhole near Futenma prompts PFAS tests
record.detail: Ginowan's sewage division received a report of white foam coming from a manhole in the Isa district that collects water from MCAS Futenma and nearby homes; city and US military took samples for PFAS testing. Marines said there had been no firefighting-foam releases.
record.attribution: Ginowan City via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Four Chinese coast guard ships enter Senkaku territorial waters
record.detail: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Uotsuri Island and Taisho islet shortly after 16:00 and left about two hours later; the Japan Coast Guard said it was the second incursion of 2026 and that no Japanese fishing boats were being pursued.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Okinawa fraud losses about ¥3.2 billion in 2025
record.detail: National Police Agency figures released Feb 12 put 2025 losses to special fraud plus SNS investment and romance scams at a record ~¥324.1 billion nationwide (+62.8%), with Okinawa losses about ¥3.2 billion.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing National Police Agency

record.title: Kyokuryukai chairman arrested for attempted extortion
record.detail: Police arrested the 71-year-old chairman of designated gang Kyokuryukai and a 45-year-old member on suspicion of attempting to extort 'settlement money' from a woman in her 50s over an August 2024 container-confinement incident.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

record.title: US Marine arrested for trespassing at elementary school
record.detail: Okinawa police arrested a 21-year-old Marine corporal from Camp Schwab on suspicion of entering an elementary school in northern Okinawa without permission; witnesses said he spoke to and followed a young girl, and police detected alcohol. He denied the allegation.

record.title: Ex-couple arrested over cashing ~¥100m of bonds stolen from vacant house
record.detail: Police allege two residents of Haebaru bought bonds that juveniles had stolen from a vacant house in Okinawa and redeemed them for about ¥100 million at a Tokyo financial institution in Aug 2025; charges include receiving stolen goods and fraud. Over ¥100 million in cash was also reportedly found at the house.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

record.title: Third arrest in stolen-bond laundering case
record.detail: A 27-year-old man from Itoman was arrested as a third suspect; police allege violations of the Act on Punishment of Organized Crimes (concealment and receipt of criminal proceeds) and fraud over roughly ¥100 million in redeemed stolen bonds, allegedly spent on dining and luxury goods.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

record.title: Naha man sentenced for receiving fraud and theft proceeds
record.detail: The Naha District Court Okinawa Branch sentenced a 34-year-old Naha man to 1 year 6 months' imprisonment and a ¥500,000 fine for knowingly receiving ¥905,000 of criminal proceeds on five occasions under the organized crime law; prosecutors had sought 2 years.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Naha District Court Okinawa Branch

record.title: Prefectural police and six lenders agree to share fraud-account data
record.detail: Okinawa Prefectural Police signed an agreement with Ryukyu Bank, Bank of Okinawa, Okinawa Kaiho Bank, Koza Shinkin, Okinawa Rokin and JA Okinawa to share details of frozen fraud-linked accounts in real time. Police cited 543 fraud cases and about ¥3.23 billion in losses in the prefecture last year.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police and participating banks

record.title: Chinese coast guard ships chase Japanese fishing boat into Senkaku waters
record.detail: Two China Coast Guard vessels entered territorial waters about 12 nautical miles southwest of Minamikojima around 05:30 while pursuing a Japanese fishing boat and stayed until 19:20 the next day; two more ships were in the contiguous zone, per Japan Coast Guard releases.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Two boats capsize off Henoko on school peace trip; 2 dead
record.detail: Two small motorboats carrying Kyoto high school students capsized off Henoko Cape near Camp Schwab at 10:10; a 17-year-old student and a captain in his 70s died. The coast guard sent 11 boats and a helicopter.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Body found after sugarcane field fire in Miyakojima
record.detail: A fire burned about 4,000 sq m of a sugarcane field in Taira, Miyakojima; a man's body was found and the 90-year-old owner could not be reached.
record.agency: Miyakojima Police Station / Miyakojima City Fire Department
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Miyakojima Police Station / Miyakojima City Fire Department

record.title: Second Chinese coast guard incursion at Senkakus in same week
record.detail: Four China Coast Guard vessels, including the pair from Monday's incursion, re-entered Japanese territorial waters shortly after 16:00 and left after about two hours; Japanese patrol ships warned them with electronic message boards, according to the Japan Coast Guard (fifth incursion of 2026).
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: US sailor gets suspended sentence for mailing magic truffles to Okinawa
record.detail: Naha District Court gave a Camp Foster-based US Navy petty officer a two-year sentence suspended for four years for trying to import 71g of psilocybin truffles by mail from the Netherlands.
record.attribution: Stars and Stripes, citing Naha District Court

record.title: Prefectural survey finds record PFAS near Kadena and Futenma
record.detail: Okinawa's environmental division reported new maximum PFAS levels, up to 2,800 ppt at Yara Hijaga in Kadena town (standard 50 ppt), with elevated levels at 31 of 44 sites around US bases including downstream of Futenma.
record.attribution: Okinawa Prefecture via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Chinese research ship surveys in Japan's EEZ near Senkakus
record.detail: The Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 22 was found about 40 miles west-northwest of Uotsuri Island extending pipe- and wire-like objects into the sea in Japan's EEZ; a Japan Coast Guard patrol ship radioed that research without Japan's consent was unacceptable.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Four armed Chinese coast guard ships briefly enter Senkaku waters
record.detail: Maritime Executive, citing a Japan Coast Guard statement, reported four China Coast Guard ships (Haijing 2303, 2302, 2401, 2307), observed with machine guns, were in territorial waters from about 06:00 to 06:20, and that Chinese vessels had been present around the Senkakus for 138 consecutive days.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via The Maritime Executive

record.title: First measles case of 2026 in Okinawa
record.detail: Okinawa Prefecture reported its first measles patient of 2026 and warned people who shared air space at locations the patient visited that they may have been exposed.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefecture Health and Medical Care Dept.

record.title: Kin town water survey finds PFAS near Camp Hansen
record.detail: Kin town's annual survey found five of 14 sites above Japan's 50 ppt standard, highest 220 ppt near Ryukyu Hospital about 730 feet from Camp Hansen; the water is not used for drinking.
record.attribution: Kin Town via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Influenza advisory lifted (week 14)
record.detail: Okinawa Prefecture lifted its influenza advisory as reports fell to 6.64 per sentinel site in week 14 (Mar 30-Apr 5), but said Yaeyama still exceeded the threshold.

record.title: Taiwanese cruise passenger caught with stimulants at Naha Port
record.detail: A 56-year-old Taiwanese national arriving on a cruise ship from Keelung was found with 1.2g of stimulants; Naha Coast Guard arrested him April 12 and customs filed charges April 27.
record.agency: Okinawa District Customs / Naha Coast Guard Office
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Naha Coast Guard Office

record.title: Chinese research vessel Kexue operates in EEZ north of Ishigaki
record.detail: The Chinese research ship Kexue was spotted about 45 miles north of Ishigaki extending wire-like objects until April 17, then stayed in Japan's EEZ until leaving westward early on April 29, the third such case in a month, per the Japan Coast Guard.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Chinese destroyer and frigate pass 80 km south of Hateruma
record.detail: Japan's Joint Staff Office reported destroyer Baotou and frigate Huanggang about 80 km south of Hateruma Island on April 22, part of movements through the southwest region from April 19.
record.attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via USNI News

record.title: Fatal fire at gang office flat in Okinawa City
record.detail: A pre-dawn fire gutted a fourth-floor flat in Moromizato used as an office of designated gang Kyokuryukai; one person died and police were checking whether it was the group's chairman, who could not be reached.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Russian submarine and warships transit near Yonaguni
record.detail: Japan's Joint Staff Office reported a Russian group (submarine Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, corvette Gromkiy, a tug) sailing about 50 km south of Yonaguni on April 21, and a second group (corvettes Sovershenny and Rezkiy, oiler Pechenga) passing between Yonaguni and Iriomote into the East China Sea around midnight on April 22.
record.attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via USNI News

record.title: FY2025 scrambles: Southwestern Air Defense Force handles 348
record.detail: Japan's Joint Staff annual report says ASDF fighters scrambled 595 times in FY2025 (about 366 against Chinese aircraft), with the Okinawa-based Southwestern Air Defense Force conducting 348; it cites a Chinese coast guard helicopter entering airspace around the Senkakus in May 2025.
record.srcname: Japan Ministry of Defense Joint Staff

record.title: Survey finds PFAS up to 3,000 ppt downstream of Futenma
record.detail: Okinawa's groundwater surveys found PFAS at 28 of 40 sites near MCAS Futenma, peaking at 3,000 ppt at Ijunga spring, and up to 400 ppt near Camp Kinser; the prefecture said the base is highly probably the source.
record.attribution: Okinawa Prefecture via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Prefecture issues school-trip safety notice after capsizing
record.detail: Okinawa Prefecture asked organizers of school trips to adopt safety measures to prevent a recurrence after the fatal capsizing of boats carrying an out-of-prefecture high school group.

record.title: Marine dies in motorcycle-taxi crash on Route 58 near Camp Kinser
record.detail: A 21-year-old Marine riding south on Route 58 in Urasoe's Yafuso district collided with a turning taxi at 00:45 near Camp Kinser's Gate 2 and was declared dead around 01:30, police and the Marine Corps said.

record.title: Two US Marines arrested for hotel break-in and drunk driving
record.detail: Okinawa police arrested two Marines on Sunday, one on suspicion of breaking into a hotel and the other for suspected drunk driving; both denied the allegations. Xinhua noted Okinawa police handled over 100 criminal cases involving US personnel in 2025.

record.title: Second, unrelated measles case in Okinawa
record.detail: Okinawa Prefecture reported its second measles case of 2026, not linked to the first, and warned people who may have been exposed.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefecture Health and Medical Care Dept.

record.title: Four Chinese coast guard ships enter waters off Uotsuri
record.detail: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Uotsuri Island between 4:15 and 16:35 and left around 18:00, the first such entry since April 28, Jiji Press reported.

record.title: Aichi man re-arrested over cash-card fraud against elderly women in Yomitan, Chatan
record.detail: Okinawa police re-arrested a 21-year-old Aichi company employee who allegedly posed as a municipal official offering insurance refunds, obtained cash cards from two women in their 70s and withdrew about ¥450,000 on April 8.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station

record.title: Four Vietnamese arrested for shipping 1,936 protected hermit crabs
record.detail: Naha police arrested four Vietnamese nationals for allegedly shipping 1,936 land hermit crabs, a designated natural monument, out of the prefecture from a Naha convenience store under the Cultural Properties Protection Act; a courier had alerted police.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

record.title: 250kg US bomb defused in Urasoe; 850 evacuated, monorail halted
record.detail: The JGSDF defused a US-made 250kg bomb near Urasoe-Maeda station; about 850 people were evacuated within 283m and Yui Rail was suspended between Shuri and Urasoe for about 2h45m.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Japan Ground Self-Defense Force

record.title: US soldier referred to prosecutors over alleged sexual assault
record.detail: Okinawa Prefectural Police referred a Kadena-based US Army air-defense soldier in his 20s to the Naha prosecutors over an alleged April sexual assault and injury of a woman outdoors on Okinawa's main island; he also allegedly hit a roadside barrier and failed to report it.
record.attribution: Okinawa police via Stars and Stripes

record.title: TB cluster at adult day-care facility in southern Okinawa
record.detail: The prefecture announced a tuberculosis cluster at an adult day-care facility under the Southern Health Center: as of May 11, 5 active cases and 27 infections.

record.title: Tropical Storm Jangmi crosses Okinawa
record.detail: Jiji reported a maximum gust of 30.7 m/s in Naha on June 1 as Jangmi was forecast to cross the main island; JMA urged residents to avoid nonessential travel. Wikipedia's compilation lists 17 injuries and 82,921 evacuated across five municipalities in Okinawa.
record.attribution: JMA via Jiji Press; injury/evacuation figures from Wikipedia

record.title: Jangmi cuts power in 27 Okinawa municipalities
record.detail: Power outages affected 27 municipalities in Okinawa Prefecture as Tropical Storm Jangmi crossed the islands, according to Wikipedia's storm article.

record.title: Tsunami advisory reaches Okinawa after M7.8 Philippines quake
record.detail: JMA issued a tsunami advisory from Ibaraki to Okinawa after a magnitude 7.8 quake off the southern Philippines, earlier warning of up to 1 m for Miyako and Yaeyama; a minor tsunami was observed on Okinawa's main island around 12:18.

record.title: Three Chinese nationals held over underground bank laundering Okinawa fraud money
record.detail: A joint Tokyo MPD-Okinawa police task force arrested two Tokyo-based Chinese nationals on June 8 for unlicensed currency exchange (Banking Act) and a third on June 15 for fraud; police suspect special-fraud proceeds, including ¥5 million taken from an 80-year-old Okinawa resident, were laundered via the yuan-exchange scheme.
record.agency: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department / Okinawa Prefectural Police
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing MPD-Okinawa joint investigation

record.title: First UXO disposal on Yonaguni: four WWII navy bombs
record.detail: Four 250kg Imperial Japanese Navy bombs found offshore in 2020 were disposed of underwater near Kubura port, with a 3km diving ban and vessel limits.

record.title: Four US servicemen arrested in two days in Okinawa
record.detail: Okinawa police arrested two US servicemen for alleged drunk driving on June 13 and, on June 14, one for an assault at a restaurant that injured a person's head and one for trespassing in an apartment building.

record.title: Level 4 heavy-rain and landslide warnings on Okinawa Island; Tonaki 73mm/h
record.detail: The Okinawa Meteorological Observatory issued heavy-rain warnings for Tonaki and Motobu and landslide warnings for Urasoe, Nanjo, Yaese, Kitanakagusuku and Onna; Tonaki logged 73mm in an hour and a record 205.5mm in 6 hours. Naha had 382.5mm from June 9-16.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Meteorological Observatory (JMA)

record.title: Floods and landslides across Okinawa Island; cars submerged
record.detail: Heavy rain submerged three cars in about 1m of water in Okinawa City, stranded two on Route 54 in Itoman and flooded Route 449 in Motobu; landslides hit Miyagi Island (Uruma), Nakijin and Urasoe. Evacuation centres opened; no deaths reported.

record.title: Resolute Dragon 26 drills include Sakishima disaster-relief training
record.detail: Japan's defense ministry said the Japan-US Resolute Dragon 26 exercise (June 20-30) would set up command centers at Camp Foster and Camp Kinser and hold disaster-relief drills on Miyako (about 70 personnel), Ishigaki (about 50) and Yonaguni (about 50) with Ospreys, CH-47s, CH-53s and C-130s.
record.place: Camp Foster / Camp Kinser; Miyako, Ishigaki, Yonaguni

record.title: Trash burning spreads, five houses burn down in Nago
record.detail: Five homes in the Umusa area of Nago were destroyed after a resident's trash fire spread; no injuries were reported.
record.agency: Nago Fire Department / Nago Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Nago Fire Department / Nago Police Station

record.title: Fake-police scam takes ¥200,000 in crypto from northern Okinawa woman
record.detail: Callers posing as out-of-prefecture police and prosecutors told a woman in her 40s her cash card was found at a suspect's home and had her buy and send about ¥200,000 in cryptocurrency, Nago police said.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station

record.title: Central Okinawa firm loses ¥27.3m to CEO-impersonation email
record.detail: An employee of a company in central Okinawa wired ¥27.3 million after an email in the CEO's name led her to a LINE group demanding payment, Urasoe police said, urging firms to verify remittance rules.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Urasoe Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Urasoe Police Station

record.title: Chinese national caught near fishing port as fake-police scam collector in Kin
record.detail: Ishikawa police arrested a 48-year-old Chinese national on July 1 (re-arrested July 22) as the alleged cash collector in a fake-police scam in which a Kin man in his 40s left ¥1.5 million in his mailbox; he tried to flee toward a fishing port when a second ¥2 million pickup was staked out.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ishikawa Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ishikawa Police Station

record.title: Hermit-crab poachers fined; 3,869 crabs taken
record.detail: Four Vietnamese nationals were fined ¥300,000-400,000 each by summary order after prosecutors charged them over collecting and shipping 3,869 protected land hermit crabs, many juveniles.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Naha District Public Prosecutors Office

record.title: M6.1-6.4 quake northwest of Miyako Island
record.detail: An offshore quake northwest of Miyakojima (about 26N 125.8E) was rated M6.4 by JMA (M6.1 by USGS), shaking Kume Island at lower 3; no tsunami warning or damage was reported.
record.attribution: JMA via SANA; USGS figure via Yeni Safak

record.title: Man arrested after violent assault at Naha seaside park
record.detail: Police arrested a 35-year-old man on suspicion of assault after a 23-year-old man was badly beaten at Wakasa Seaside Park near Naminoue Beach; off-duty US Marines gave first aid and held the suspect until police arrived.

record.title: Japan and China coast guards face off near Senkakus
record.detail: Two of four China Coast Guard ships entered waters near the Senkakus; Japan's coast guard said it forced them out by about 09:20, while China's coast guard said it had expelled the Japanese fishing boat Zuihou Maru. Tokyo called the entry a violation of international law.
record.attribution: Japan Coast Guard and China Coast Guard statements via The Defense Post (AFP)

record.title: Typhoon Bavi hits Sakishima islands
record.detail: Bavi (950 hPa, up to 40 m/s sustained) brought gusts of 40 m/s on Miyako and 34 m/s on Ishigaki early July 11; Shimoji Island recorded 154.5 mm of rain in 24 hours, Jiji reported.

record.title: Hand, foot and mouth disease warning issued
record.detail: Okinawa Prefecture issued a hand, foot and mouth disease warning as week 28 (Jul 6-12) reports reached 5.29 per sentinel (threshold 5.00), 127 cases from 24 sites; first warning in about two years.

record.title: Japan's first case under new 'remittance crime' law, in Tomigusuku
record.detail: Tomigusuku police referred a Tomigusuku woman in her 40s to prosecutors, the first case nationwide under the Criminal Proceeds Transfer Prevention Act's new remittance-offence provision (in force July 10). She allegedly took an Instagram 'side job', received about ¥1.75 million and forwarded it to designated accounts; her bank flagged the activity.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Tomigusuku Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Tomigusuku Police Station

record.title: Store staff stop lottery-prize fraud against elderly man
record.detail: Staff at a Tomigusuku convenience store stopped an elderly customer from buying a prepaid card (¥3,000 'handling fee') for a fake ¥700 million prize and called police; Tomigusuku Police commended them. Police said such special-fraud schemes escalate from small initial payments.

record.title: Okinawa special-fraud losses about ¥1.2 billion in first half of 2026
record.detail: National Police Agency figures put first-half 2026 special-fraud losses at a record ~¥181.6 billion nationwide, with Okinawa losses reported at about ¥1.2 billion.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing National Police Agency

record.title: Uruma teen arrested for cannabis possession
record.detail: Uruma police arrested an 18-year-old man over 2.47g of cannabis found in a store parking lot on July 9, then re-arrested him for use after a positive urine test.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Uruma Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Uruma Police Station

record.title: US consulate warns of large typhoon, closes Aug 6-7
record.detail: The US Consulate General Naha warned that a large typhoon would affect Okinawa from Aug. 6 through at least Aug. 9 with very strong winds, storm surge, heavy rain, flooding and landslides, and closed to the public Aug. 6-7.

record.title: Typhoon Dolphin strengthens near northwestern Okinawa
record.detail: JMA data showed 10-minute sustained winds of 162 km/h; gusts reached 151 km/h in Nago and at Oku (Kunigami). The prefecture reported at least five injured and partial damage to five homes; evacuation orders covered about 262,500 people across Kagoshima and Okinawa.
record.attribution: JMA and Okinawa Prefecture via The Watchers

record.title: Level 4 heavy-rain warnings for Ogimi, Higashi, Nakijin
record.detail: During Typhoon Dolphin, JMA Level 4 heavy-rain risk warnings were in effect for Ogimi, Higashi and Nakijin in northern Okinawa Island.

record.title: Level 4 storm-surge warning for Kumejima
record.detail: During Typhoon Dolphin a JMA Level 4 storm-surge risk warning was in effect for Kumejima.

record.title: Typhoon Dolphin leaves about 17,000 households without power
record.detail: About 16,920 households in 21 municipalities were without power at 17:00 JST, roughly 90% of them in northern Okinawa Island (AFP/ABC reported about 12,000-14,000 buildings the following day).

record.title: All 417 flights at Naha, Miyako, Ishigaki, Shimojishima cancelled
record.detail: All 417 scheduled flights serving Naha, Miyako, Ishigaki and Shimojishima airports on Aug. 7 were cancelled because of Typhoon Dolphin.

record.title: Pre-dawn fire at Chatan hotel; unconscious guest rescued
record.detail: Police got a report of a hotel fire in Chatan at 03:30; a Marine alerted sleeping guests and firefighters removed an unconscious 55-year-old man. Police later alleged a guest set the fire deliberately.

record.title: Man in 20s loses ¥6.7m to fake police via LINE video call
record.detail: Scammers posing as police and prosecutors showed a fake warrant over LINE video and had a self-employed man in his 20s in central Okinawa transfer about ¥6.7 million between Aug 4 and 17, Ginowan police said.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ginowan Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ginowan Police Station

record.title: Typhoon Saudel lashes Okinawa and Amami
record.detail: Saudel carried winds up to 144 km/h; a 78-year-old woman in Uruma was injured when wind knocked her down, about 150 Naha flights were cancelled, and up to 12 cm of rain was forecast for Okinawa, per JMA, FDMA and prefectural officials cited by AP.
record.attribution: AP citing JMA, FDMA, prefectural officials

record.title: About 150 Naha flights cancelled for Typhoon Saudel
record.detail: Some 150 flights to and from Naha Airport were cancelled as Typhoon Saudel passed near Okinawa, AP reported.

record.title: American tourist arrested over alleged arson at Chatan hotel
record.detail: Okinawa police arrested a 32-year-old US visitor with no fixed address on suspicion of arson and attempted murder over the Aug. 15 fire at a Chatan hotel where 18 other guests were staying; he was already in custody over an Aug. 21 break-in in Urasoe.
record.attribution: Okinawa police via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Fake arrest-warrant scam costs southern Okinawa worker ¥800,000
record.detail: A company employee in his 30s in southern Okinawa main island sent about ¥800,000 after callers posing as police and prosecutors claimed a warrant was out for him, Naha police said.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

record.title: Illegal insect traps found again in Yanbaru National Park
record.detail: The Environment Ministry and prefectural police found 16 unauthorised insect traps targeting rare species in Yanbaru (Kunigami, Ogimi, Higashi) so far in FY2026, after 25 in FY2025, and are stepping up countermeasures.
record.agency: Ministry of the Environment / Okinawa Prefectural Police
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Ministry of the Environment / Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Downpour floods roads on Ishigaki, two cars submerged
record.detail: 48.5mm fell in an hour in Maesato, Ishigaki; two cars were submerged, a road flooded about 50cm deep and was closed, and a waste facility briefly halted. The observatory linked instability to typhoons 18 and 24 nearby.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Ishigaki Local Meteorological Office (JMA)

record.title: Southwestern ASDF scrambles on Chinese Y-9 near Okinawa
record.detail: Japan's Joint Staff said a Chinese Y-9 intelligence aircraft flew over the East China Sea five days running (Sept 3-7) near Okinawa Island and the Danjo Islands; the Southwestern Air Defense Force scrambled on Sept 5. No airspace violation was reported.
record.place: East China Sea west of Okinawa Island
record.attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via AeroTime

record.title: Kanagawa man arrested as withdrawer in ¥3m refund scam on northern Okinawa couple
record.detail: Police arrested a 50-year-old Kanagawa man, suspected withdrawer for an anonymous fluid-type crime group, over a scheme posing as city staff offering care-insurance refunds that took about ¥3 million from two people in their 60s in February; he denies the charges.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Saitama man arrested over ¥46m gold-bar fake-police scam in Naha
record.detail: Police arrested a 61-year-old Saitama man accused of posing as a police officer to collect gold bullion worth about ¥46 million from a Naha man in his 70s on July 1; police are probing an anonymous fluid-type crime group link and the gold's whereabouts.
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

record.title: Camp Schwab Marine arrested for stealing car in Nago
record.detail: Nago police arrested a 21-year-old Marine lance corporal from Camp Schwab accused of stealing a car worth about ¥830,000 from a Nago parking lot; alcohol was detected and he reportedly said he took it to go to a convenience store.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station

record.title: Influenza advisory issued; Okinawa highest per-sentinel in Japan
record.detail: Okinawa issued an influenza advisory as week 36 (Aug 31-Sep 6) reached 10.34 per sentinel (455 cases from 44 sites), the highest nationwide per Ryukyu Shimpo; Yaeyama (13.33) and the southern region (13.17) were highest.
record.attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government; regional figures via Ryukyu Shimpo

record.title: Report says US told Japan in 2023 that base foam likely caused PFAS
record.detail: The Okinawa Times reported that US officials told Tokyo in December 2023 that PFAS foam used at Kadena and Futenma was likely responsible for nearby contamination, an assessment not made public; US and Japanese officials offered few details.
record.attribution: Okinawa Times via Stars and Stripes

record.title: Camp Hansen Marine arrested for drunk driving after crash in Okinawa City
record.detail: Okinawa police arrested a 22-year-old Camp Hansen Marine after a collision on Prefectural Route 23 in Ageda; a breath test showed 0.5mg/L or more of alcohol. He denies the charge.
record.agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station
record.attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station

record.detail: Canal authorities cut ship movements because El Niño rainfall shortfalls lowered water levels; further cuts are possible (UPI, The Guardian, Al Jazeera).

record.detail: The U.S. is expanding its military footprint around the canal, including interdiction of suspicious vessels (The Economist).

record.detail: Panama declared its highest nationwide alert over El Niño drought (UPI, France 24).

record.detail: An explosion at a nightclub in Trujillo injured 33 people including minors (The Guardian).

record.detail: A Cessna sightseeing flight from Pisco crashed over the Nazca Lines, killing 13 (Reuters, The Guardian).
